title: Efficacy of Yoga-Based Interventions in Reducing Inflammatory Markers in Rheumatoid Arthritis Patients
venue: Open Access Journal of Multidisciplinary Research
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune illness characterized by systemic inflammation, joint degradation, and high levels of pro-inflammatory markers such CRP, ESR, IL-6, and TNF-α. Traditional pharmaceutical treatments, while helpful, frequently have limitations such as adverse effects and unpredictable long-term efficacy. This evaluation looks at the effectiveness of yoga-based therapies as an additional therapy for lowering inflammatory markers in RA patients. A thorough review of randomized controlled trials and clinical studies reveals that regular yoga practice, which includes physical postures (asanas), breathing techniques (pranayama), and meditation, can significantly reduce inflammatory biomarkers while improving clinical outcomes such as pain, fatigue, and quality of life. Yoga appears to affect neuroendocrine function and immunological response, predominantly via stress reduction and parasympathetic activation. While the existing evidence is promising, further large-scale, well-designed trials are required to standardize techniques and prove long-term effects. This review emphasizes yoga as a safe, low-cost, and holistic strategy that supplements current RA treatments by targeting both physiological and psychological processes implicated in chronic inflammation.
